No teaching analogy appears in any section.

The Filipino subsection explains sentence roles, speaker, listener, ownership, and gender with short Filipino sentences. The Filipino worked explanations use the same simple language.

checked: Pronoun and antecedent are defined before use; singular and plural receive meanings before the agreement cases. Filipino role explanations precede the examples, and person and inclusion sets are explained before they are tested.

The lesson teaches how to choose by referent and role. Ang identifies the featured person, ng identifies an owner or actor, and sa identifies a recipient; local examples and worked decisions show how these differ.

Conditions cover unknown gender, singular verbs after everyone, collective unit/member meanings, and-joining, mixed or/nor editing, inclusive/exclusive forms, polite kayo, and the absence of a gender distinction in siya. Fronted akin explicitly does not require sa.
